findings.title: Pin and verify the installer before executing it
findings.whyItBreaks: Every build downloads mutable content from a remote URL and immediately executes it as root. A compromised or changed endpoint can silently inject arbitrary code into the produced image.

findings.title: Pin and verify the remotely executed installer
findings.whyItBreaks: Every image build executes whatever bytes the mutable URL serves. A compromised endpoint, DNS path, or changed installer can run arbitrary code in the build and alter the resulting image without a reviewed source change.

findings.title: Fail the build when the installer download fails
findings.whyItBreaks: The shell reports a pipeline's final command status. If curl fails before emitting data, `sh` receives empty input and exits successfully, so the image can build without the intended installation. curl also lacks `--fail`, allowing HTTP error bodies to be treated as installer input.

findings.title: Pin and verify the downloaded installer before executing it
findings.whyItBreaks: The image build executes whatever bytes this mutable external URL returns as root. A replaced or compromised response can modify the resulting image and its build environment without a version, checksum, or signature verification boundary.

findings.title: Fail the build when the installer download fails
findings.whyItBreaks: With a DNS, TLS, or connection failure, curl exits nonzero but sh receives empty input and exits zero. Because the shell pipeline reports the final command's status, Docker records this RUN layer as successful and produces an image with the installation silently skipped.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors in LoadOrDefault
findings.whyItBreaks: Discarding ErrMissing makes a missing key return "", identical to a key whose stored value is intentionally empty. As an exported API, every caller is forced to treat lookup failure as valid data and can proceed with missing required state.

findings.title: Preserve the missing-key signal
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns ErrMissing for an absent key, but this exported API discards that error and returns "", identical to the valid value for a present key mapped to an empty string. Callers therefore cannot safely distinguish missing data from stored data.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key information in LoadOrDefault
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns ErrMissing for an absent key, but this discards it and returns "". A map entry intentionally storing "" produces the identical result, so callers of this exported API cannot distinguish absent data from a real empty value.

findings.title: Wait for result sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: Each send now runs in an untracked goroutine, so Run can return before any result is delivered. A caller that closes results after Run returns will panic in a delayed sender; callers that consume results after the call can also observe incomplete output.

findings.title: Wait for result sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: Each send now runs in an untracked goroutine, so Run may return before any result is sent. A caller that closes results after Run returns can cause these goroutines to panic with "send on closed channel"; callers also can no longer use Run returning as proof that all jobs were processed.

findings.title: Wait for result sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: Run previously returned only after every result had been sent. It now returns immediately after spawning goroutines; a caller that closes results after Run returns can cause the remaining goroutines to panic with "send on closed channel", and callers can observe incomplete results at return.

findings.title: Require admin status and tenant ownership for deletion
findings.whyItBreaks: Using || returns true for any non-admin whose tenant matches the record, and for any admin targeting a record in another tenant. This bypasses the prior administrator requirement and tenant isolation for the exported deletion authorization decision.

findings.title: Require admin status before allowing record deletion
findings.whyItBreaks: For a non-admin session whose tenant matches the record (`isAdmin=false`, equal tenant IDs), this now returns `true` via `false || true`. The prior policy required both administrator authority and tenant matching, so this authorizes deletion without the required privilege.

findings.title: Require admin status and tenant membership before deletion
findings.whyItBreaks: Using || authorizes any non-admin whose tenant matches the record, whereas the prior policy required both admin status and tenant membership. It also authorizes an admin for records in another tenant.

findings.title: Preserve invalid-settings failures before saving
findings.whyItBreaks: Malformed or schema-invalid stored settings previously threw, so updateFontSize never invoked save. The new catch returns defaults instead; updateFontSize then changes fontSize and saves that value, silently overwriting the invalid settings and losing any recoverable data such as the user's theme.

findings.title: Preserve invalid-settings errors before saving
findings.whyItBreaks: The catch converts both JSON parse and schema-validation failures into real-looking settings. updateFontSize then changes the font size and invokes save, so input such as {"theme":"dark"} is saved as {"theme":"light","fontSize":<size>} instead of failing without a write. This silently loses the valid theme field that was present in the malformed record.

findings.title: Preserve parse failures before saving settings
findings.whyItBreaks: Malformed or schema-invalid persisted settings previously threw and prevented updateFontSize from calling save. The new catch returns defaults, so updateFontSize changes the default font size and saves it at line 22, overwriting the original data while erasing the parse failure.

findings.title: Use the requested branch commit for report artifacts
findings.whyItBreaks: For any branch whose ref differs from `verified`, `builtFrom` contains the requested branch commit but `artifacts` are fetched from the verified commit. Consumers receive a self-inconsistent report and can associate artifacts with the wrong build.

findings.title: Keep artifacts tied to the reported commit
findings.whyItBreaks: When `build.ref(branch)` and `build.ref("verified")` differ, `builtFrom` reports the branch commit while `artifacts` are loaded from the verified commit. Consumers receive a self-contradictory BuildReport and can present or act on artifacts that were not built from the reported ref.

findings.title: Fetch artifacts from the requested branch
findings.whyItBreaks: For buildReport(build, "feature"), builtFrom is the commit resolved from "feature", but artifacts are always fetched from the unrelated "verified" ref. The report can therefore claim a build's artifacts while returning another build's artifacts.

findings.title: Restore the requested result limit
findings.whyItBreaks: For every positive limit, this returns every reversed entry rather than at most `limit`. `renderFeed` passes 20 and writes each returned item into a 20-slot array, which expands the returned feed beyond 20 entries when input contains more than 20 items.

findings.title: Apply the limit before returning sorted entries
findings.whyItBreaks: For every positive limit, this returns all entries rather than at most limit. renderFeed passes 20 at src/feed.ts:9; with 21 inputs, its loop writes index 20 and expands the 20-slot result to 21 entries.

findings.title: Honor the supplied positive limit
findings.whyItBreaks: For any positive limit, this returns every reversed entry instead of at most `limit`. For example, `renderFeed` passes 20, but an input of 21 entries produces a 21-element result because its loop copies the uncapped page.

findings.title: Count only emitted manifest entries
findings.whyItBreaks: When any entry is stale, the output contains only `live` rows but `# entry-count` is still derived from `entries.length`. Consumers relying on that header will observe a count larger than the number of manifest records.

findings.title: Count only emitted manifest entries
findings.whyItBreaks: Filtering stale entries removes their rows, but the unchanged header call still receives entries.length. For input with one live and one stale entry, the manifest declares `# entry-count: 2` while emitting one row, producing an internally inconsistent manifest for consumers that rely on its count.

findings.title: Count only emitted manifest entries
findings.whyItBreaks: When any entry has stale=true, it is omitted from rows but entries.length is still written as # entry-count. Consumers relying on that header will see more declared entries than serialized entries.

findings.title: Preserve the viewer read-only path

findings.title: Return the file close error from Save
findings.whyItBreaks: On a successful Flush, a failure reported by f.Close is now discarded by the deferred call and Save returns nil. Filesystems can report delayed write failures at close, so callers of this exported function cannot distinguish a successfully persisted file from a failed save.

findings.title: Propagate output-file close errors
findings.whyItBreaks: After a successful Flush, the deferred f.Close() error is discarded. A delayed output or filesystem error during Close therefore returns nil from the exported Save API, whereas the prior implementation returned that error; callers can falsely treat a failed save as successful.

findings.title: Iterate through the page's end bound
findings.whyItBreaks: The half-open bound returned by _window_bounds is [start, end), but range(start, end - 1) excludes index end - 1. Every nonempty page loses its last row; a one-row page becomes empty, so render_page and summarize silently omit data.

findings.title: Include the page's final row
findings.whyItBreaks: range(start, end - 1) excludes index end - 1. A one-row page returns [], and every nonempty page omits its last row; render_page and summarize therefore silently drop data.

findings.title: Include the page's final row
findings.whyItBreaks: range(start, end - 1) excludes index end - 1. A one-row page returns an empty list, and every other non-empty page loses its last row; render_page and summarize therefore omit displayed data.

findings.title: Restore fresh-cache reads
findings.whyItBreaks: A newly stored entry has age below ttlMs, so this condition is false and get() deletes it and returns null. Once an entry is older than ttlMs, the condition becomes true and get() returns the expired value indefinitely.

findings.title: Do not splice while iterating completed jobs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing an item shifts the next job into the current index, but forEach advances to the next index. Therefore `pruneDone([{id:"a",done:true},{id:"b",done:true}])` leaves job b in the result.

findings.title: Return cache entries only before their TTL expires
findings.whyItBreaks: A newly stored entry has elapsed time below ttlMs, so the changed `>` condition deletes it and returns null. Once elapsed time exceeds ttlMs, it instead returns the expired value indefinitely.

findings.title: Remove all completed jobs without skipping adjacent entries
findings.whyItBreaks: Splicing while `forEach` advances its index skips the item that shifts into the removed item's position. For `[done:a, done:b, pending:c]`, removing `a` makes `b` shift to index 0, then iteration proceeds to `c` at index 1; `b` remains in the returned queue.

findings.title: Restore the non-expired TTL comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: An entry retrieved immediately after set has age 0, so for a positive ttlMs this condition is false and get deletes it and returns null. Once an entry is older than ttlMs, the condition becomes true, so get returns stale data indefinitely.

findings.title: Do not splice while iterating completed jobs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing an element shifts the next job into the current index, but forEach advances to the next index. For [done, done], the first job is removed and the second is skipped, so pruneDone returns a completed job.

findings.title: Preserve the empty-input average value
findings.whyItBreaks: For an empty array, reduce returns 0 and division by rows.length produces NaN. The prior implementation returned 0, so callers now receive a non-numeric sentinel where the public function previously supplied a usable number.

findings.title: Do not mutate the caller’s rows while finding busiest
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.prototype.sort mutates rows in place. A caller that retains its input order will have it silently reordered after calling busiest(); the prior implementation explicitly sorted a copied array.

findings.title: Preserve the empty-input average behavior
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the empty-array guard makes averageAmount([]) evaluate 0 / 0 and return NaN, replacing its prior defined result of 0.

findings.title: Avoid mutating the caller's rows
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.prototype.sort mutates its receiver. Calling busiest(rows) now permanently reorders the caller-owned array, whereas the previous implementation sorted a defensive copy.

findings.title: Restore the empty-input average result
findings.whyItBreaks: For an empty array, reduce produces 0 and division by rows.length produces NaN. The prior implementation returned 0, so callers can no longer use the function's result as a valid numeric aggregate.

findings.title: Avoid mutating rows while finding the busiest row
findings.whyItBreaks: `Array.prototype.sort` mutates its receiver. Calling `busiest(rows)` now reorders the caller's array, whereas the previous defensive copy preserved its order.

findings.title: Sort scores with a numeric comparator
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.sort() without a comparator orders numbers as strings. For scores 9, 100, and 8 it produces [100, 8, 9] before reverse, so topPlayers(..., 1) uses cutoff 9 and can return the first 9-point player instead of the 100-point player.

findings.title: Sort scores numerically before deriving the cutoff
findings.whyItBreaks: Array#sort without a comparator converts numbers to strings. For scores [9, 80, 100], rankScores returns [9, 80, 100] after reverse; topPlayers(..., 1) therefore uses 9 as its cutoff and can return the first input player rather than the 100-score player.

findings.title: Restore numeric descending score sorting
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.sort() without a comparator sorts scores as strings. For input ordered as scores [9, 8, 100], it produces [100, 8, 9], then reverse() produces [9, 8, 100]. With n=1, the cutoff becomes 9, and topPlayers keeps both 9 and 100 before slice(0, 1) returns the 9-point player instead of the 100-point player.

findings.title: Restore constant-time signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: Using == can reveal information about matching signature prefixes through comparison timing. This verification result controls whether handle() accepts and processes an authenticated webhook, making the HMAC secret susceptible to a remote timing-oracle attack.

findings.title: Restore constant-time webhook signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: String equality may stop at the first mismatched character, exposing comparison timing for attacker-controlled signatures. This can allow a remote attacker to progressively infer the HMAC and submit a forged webhook that reaches processor(payload).

findings.title: Restore constant-time webhook signature verification
findings.whyItBreaks: String equality may return after the first differing character, leaking how much of an attacker-supplied HMAC matches through response timing. An attacker can use that oracle to recover a valid signature and reach processor(payload) without possessing the secret.

findings.title: Keep ledger and balance updates in one transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The ledger insert commits when the transaction scope ends at line 23. If either balance UPDATE then fails, the transfer returns an error after a committed ledger row; if the credit fails after the debit, balances are also left inconsistent. Previously all three writes rolled back together.

findings.title: Keep balance updates in the ledger transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The ledger INSERT is committed when the transaction exits at line 23, then the debit and credit run outside it. If either balance update fails, the transfer leaves a committed ledger record with unchanged or only partially updated balances; if the credit fails after the debit succeeds, funds are effectively lost.

findings.title: Keep balance updates in the ledger transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: Exiting the transaction commits the ledger insert before either balance update runs. If a later update fails, the transfer leaves a committed ledger record with unchanged or only partially updated account balances.

findings.title: Keep billing-day computation in UTC
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous exported behavior derived the day in UTC. This now derives it from the process timezone, so the same instant can be assigned to a different billing day by different deployments; for example, 2026-01-01T00:30:00Z becomes 2025-12-31 under America/Los_Angeles instead of the prior 2026-01-01.

findings.title: Preserve UTC when deriving a billing day
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation explicitly bucketed each instant by UTC date. This now uses local-time getters, so the same instant can receive different billing keys by deployment timezone; for example, 2026-09-05T00:30:00Z becomes 2026-09-04 in America/Los_Angeles instead of 2026-09-05. That splits or misclassifies billing records near midnight.

findings.title: Keep billing-day calculation in UTC
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation explicitly used UTC fields. For example, in America/Los_Angeles, new Date("2026-01-01T00:30:00Z") now produces "2025-12-31" instead of "2026-01-01". Billing dates and sameBillingDay results consequently vary by process/server timezone.

findings.title: Keep tenant in the memo key
findings.whyItBreaks: After tenant A reads account X, a read for tenant B and account X hits the same memo entry at line 15 and returns tenant A's Profile without calling fetchProfile. This leaks cross-tenant profile data and produces an incorrect result.

findings.title: Include tenant in the cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: The module-level cache is keyed only by account. After a request for tenant A and account X stores A's Profile, a request for tenant B and account X returns that cached A profile at line 16 without calling fetchProfile. This breaks tenant isolation and can disclose the cached tenant's profile data.

findings.title: Include tenant in the memoization key
findings.whyItBreaks: After reading account `shared` for tenant A, a request for the same account under tenant B finds the `shared` cache entry at line 15 and returns tenant A's Profile at line 16 without calling `fetchProfile` for tenant B. This leaks profile data across tenant boundaries.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key failures
findings.whyItBreaks: A missing entry now returns "", which is indistinguishable from a legitimately stored empty string. loadAll consequently emits an empty result element instead of reporting that a requested key is absent.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors from load
findings.whyItBreaks: A missing key previously threw, but now returns "", which is indistinguishable from a stored empty value. `loadAll` consequently returns partial-looking successful results instead of propagating the missing-key failure.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors from load
findings.whyItBreaks: A missing key previously threw; it now returns `""`, which is a valid stored value. `loadAll` therefore emits an empty string for a missing key rather than signaling invalid input, and external callers of exported `load` cannot distinguish failure from a legitimately empty value.

findings.title: Restore compatibility for existing Config callers
findings.whyItBreaks: Config is exported. Existing TypeScript callers supplying the previous required shape `{ maxAttempts, timeoutMs }` now fail type checking because `retries` and `timeout` are required. Untyped JavaScript callers instead pass `undefined` for `timeout`; `Date.now() + undefined` is NaN, so the deadline predicate never expires and retry ignores its prior timeout.

findings.title: Propagate retryBackground failure to its caller
findings.whyItBreaks: Every exception from fn, including the final failed attempt, is discarded and the exported function returns normal void after exhaustion or deadline expiry. Callers therefore cannot distinguish a successful callback from one that failed on every attempt.

findings.title: Preserve the existing Config fields
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing TypeScript callers of the exported retry API that pass `{ maxAttempts, timeoutMs }` no longer typecheck because `timeoutMs` was removed and unrelated `retries` became required. JavaScript callers receive `undefined` for `config.timeout`; `Date.now() + undefined` is NaN, so the deadline predicate never stops retries.

findings.title: Surface exhausted background retry failures
findings.whyItBreaks: If every invocation throws, retryBackground catches every error and returns `undefined`, exactly as it does after a successful attempt. As a new exported API, this forces callers to treat failed work as successful and prevents error handling or retry status reporting.

findings.title: Preserve the existing Config fields
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing TypeScript callers of retry using { maxAttempts, timeoutMs } no longer type-check because timeoutMs was removed and retries/timeout are now required. Existing JavaScript callers compute Date.now() + undefined, making the deadline NaN; the guard at line 10 is always false and the configured timeout is bypassed.

findings.title: Propagate exhausted retryBackground failures
findings.whyItBreaks: Every callback exception is discarded. Once retries are exhausted or the deadline is reached, retryBackground returns void—the same result as success—so callers cannot detect or handle failure.

findings.title: Handle numeric Field values before reading length
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed public prop type permits `value={123}`, but numbers have no `length`; this renders `len=undefined` (and TypeScript rejects the property access on `string | number`).

findings.title: Handle numeric field values before reading length
findings.whyItBreaks: `FieldProps` now permits `number`, but `number` has no `length`. TypeScript will reject this access; if transpiled without type checking, `<Field value={42}>` renders `len=undefined` instead of a numeric length.

findings.title: Handle numeric values before computing their length
findings.whyItBreaks: `FieldProps` now publicly accepts `number`, but numbers have no `length`; `<Field value={42} />` renders `len=undefined` (and fails TypeScript checking).

findings.title: Retain a sufficient buffer for Git patch output
findings.whyItBreaks: `git()` produces the full review patch at line 140. Without `maxBuffer`, Node's `spawnSync` default 1 MiB output cap aborts reviews whose textual diff exceeds that size, preventing the check and review from being posted.

findings.title: Restore the Git diff buffer limit
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer restores spawnSync's 1 MiB default. The git() call at line 140 captures the complete PR patch, so a diff over 1 MiB causes spawnSync to fail before any review is submitted. The previous 64 MiB limit and the unchanged gh helpers show this path was intentionally sized for review payloads.

findings.title: Restore the Git diff buffer limit
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer changes spawnSync from the prior 64 MiB limit to Node's 1 MiB default. The git helper is used to collect the full PR patch at line 140; a diff larger than 1 MiB terminates with a maxBuffer error (and nonzero/null status), causing the entire review action to fail instead of posting a review.

findings.title: Restore the read-only sandbox
findings.whyItBreaks: runCodex executes Codex in opts.repoPath and supplies the prompt on stdin. Removing `-s read-only` makes sandbox behavior inherit CLI configuration/defaults, including write-capable modes, so a review prompt can create, modify, or delete files in the repository being reviewed.

findings.title: Keep reviewer executions in the read-only sandbox
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing `-s read-only` delegates the sandbox choice to Codex configuration/defaults. In configurations that resolve to `workspace-write`, the prompt passed to this exported runner can now alter files under `opts.repoPath`; a review run processing untrusted repository content is therefore no longer constrained to inspection.

findings.title: Restore the read-only Codex sandbox
findings.whyItBreaks: Without the explicit `-s read-only`, `codex exec` resolves its configured/default sandbox; trusted projects can resolve to `workspace-write`. Since this process runs with `opts.repoPath` as its cwd and supplies the review prompt directly to the model, model-generated commands can now modify the repository under review.

findings.title: Restore merge-base diffing for PR revisions
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_BASE_SHA is the current target-branch tip after a PR branch diverged, `git diff baseSha HEAD` includes target-only commits as inverse changes rather than the PR's changes from the merge-base. It also ignores the supported PR_HEAD_SHA override, so the bundle can claim one head SHA while reviewing the checkout's different HEAD.

findings.title: Diff the PR from its merge base
findings.whyItBreaks: PR_BASE_SHA may be the current target-branch tip rather than the PR branch point. When target-branch commits exist after the PR diverged, `git diff baseSha HEAD` includes those unrelated changes (and can represent them as deletions), so the review bundle and changed-file list no longer describe the PR.

findings.title: Use PR_HEAD_SHA for the review bundle diff
findings.whyItBreaks: The patch and changed-file set now always use the checkout's HEAD, while the review and check run are posted to `headSha`, which can come from PR_HEAD_SHA. If HEAD differs from that configured SHA, Needlefish analyzes one revision but attaches its result to another PR revision.

findings.title: Diff from the merge base, not the current base tip
findings.whyItBreaks: For an out-of-date PR, PR_BASE_SHA can be a descendant of the branch point. `git diff baseSha HEAD` then includes base-branch-only changes as deletions, so the reviewer analyzes and may comment on changes not made by the PR. The previous implementation explicitly derived the merge base from baseSha and headSha.

findings.title: Use headSha rather than checkout HEAD for the patch
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_HEAD_SHA differs from the workspace checkout (for example, a PR job checked out at a merge ref), this builds `bundle.patch` from HEAD but labels the bundle and posts the review/check against headSha. Findings can therefore describe different code from the commit being reviewed; inline review comments may be rejected and the catch path posts only a summary.

findings.title: Preserve literal bundle content in the review prompt
findings.whyItBreaks: String.prototype.replace interprets $&, $`, and $' in a string replacement. bundle.patch is included in JSON.stringify(bundle), so a reviewed patch containing (for example) $& is rewritten to {{BUNDLE}} before runCodex receives the review prompt, corrupting the review input.

findings.title: Preserve literal findings and patch in the critic prompt
findings.whyItBreaks: Both candidate findings and bundle.patch are untrusted text passed as string replacements. Replacement tokens in either value are expanded by String.prototype.replace; for example, $& in the patch becomes {{PATCH}}. The critic can therefore receive a malformed diff or findings payload and produce an incorrect verdict.

findings.title: Use function replacements for dynamic prompt content
findings.whyItBreaks: String.replace interprets $&, $`, $', and $$ in a string replacement. Bundle JSON, Codex findings, and especially arbitrary source patches can legitimately contain these sequences; for example, a patch containing $& is replaced by the template marker rather than preserved. The review/critic prompts therefore receive corrupted input and can produce an incorrect review.

findings.title: Keep interpolated prompt data literal
findings.whyItBreaks: String.prototype.replace treats $&, $`, $', and $$ specially when given a string replacement. A patch or bundle containing $& is changed into the placeholder text, while $` or $' duplicates surrounding prompt content. The review and critic prompts therefore no longer receive the original bundle, findings, or patch whenever those normal source-text sequences occur.

findings.title: Pin fallback review to the scanned commit
findings.whyItBreaks: When the first review POST fails (for example, due to an inline-comment validation error), this fallback omits commit_id. GitHub then defaults the review to the PR's most recent commit. If the PR head advanced while Needlefish was reviewing the captured headSha, the stale verdict is posted against the newer, unscanned commit instead of the commit used to generate it.

findings.title: Preserve the reviewed SHA in the fallback request
findings.whyItBreaks: When the primary POST fails and the PR head advances before the fallback runs, omitting commit_id makes GitHub attach the review to the PR's newest commit, while this run analyzed the earlier headSha. A REQUEST_CHANGES review can therefore block code that was never reviewed. GitHub documents that an omitted commit_id defaults to the most recent PR commit.

findings.title: Keep fallback reviews bound to the reviewed commit
findings.whyItBreaks: When the JSON review request fails (for example, due to an inline-comment validation error), this fallback omits commit_id. GitHub then defaults the review to the PR's most recent commit. If a new commit is pushed while the review is running, findings computed for headSha are posted as a review of that newer, unreviewed commit.

findings.title: Reject malformed finding records
findings.whyItBreaks: Invalid severity/category and required-field or location failures no longer reach the caller as malformed output. They are returned as apparently real P1/bug findings with empty metadata or line 0, so callers cannot distinguish a model/output failure from a legitimate finding.

findings.title: Retain the strict compatibility path
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the exported strict parameter breaks TypeScript callers using normalizeReview(raw, false). JavaScript callers still pass the argument but it is ignored, changing their previous lenient behavior of dropping malformed findings into returning fabricated fallback findings.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of fabricating P1 reports
findings.whyItBreaks: A top-level-valid payload such as `{ findings: [{}] }` now becomes a normal Finding with severity P1, category bug, empty file/details, and line 0. Previously it raised a malformed-output error. Callers can no longer distinguish an invalid model response from a genuine low-severity finding.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of fabricating defaults
findings.whyItBreaks: A malformed finding such as `{ severity: "P9", file: "", lineStart: 0 }` now becomes a seemingly valid P1/bug finding with an empty file and line 0. `normalizeReview` returns it to its caller, which can no longer distinguish invalid model output from a real review finding.

findings.title: Retain the strict normalization overload
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the exported `strict` parameter breaks existing TypeScript callers of `normalizeReview(raw, false)`. JavaScript callers also lose the documented behavior of dropping malformed findings; they now receive fabricated default findings instead.

findings.title: Restore explicit repository selection for manual dispatch
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is empty and this is the first step, before actions/checkout creates a repository context. `gh pr view <number>` therefore cannot infer which repository owns the PR after `-R "$REPO"` was removed. Its failed command substitution is written as empty head/base outputs, so the checkout no longer reliably checks out the requested PR.

findings.title: Restore explicit repository resolution for manual PR runs
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is empty, so this branch runs before the Checkout PR head step. Without -R "$REPO" (or GH_REPO), gh pr view has no checked-out Git remote from which to infer the repository. It cannot resolve the PR SHAs, leaving the downstream checkout without the requested head revision.

findings.title: Retain an explicit repository for manual PR lookups
findings.whyItBreaks: For workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is empty and this branch runs before actions/checkout. `gh pr view <number>` therefore has neither a checked-out repository nor GH_REPO/--repo context. On a clean runner, gh cannot identify the target repository; its failed command substitution is written as empty head/base outputs, so checkout/review cannot operate on the requested PR.

findings.title: Reject incomplete review payloads
findings.whyItBreaks: Missing or wrongly typed required fields previously raised a malformed-review error; they now become empty strings/arrays. An exported caller cannot distinguish an invalid reviewer response from a legitimate zero-finding review, so it may treat failed review generation as a clean result.

findings.title: Preserve errors for malformed review output
findings.whyItBreaks: Missing or incorrectly typed required top-level fields now become an empty summary with no findings, checks, or residual risks. Callers of this exported API can no longer distinguish malformed reviewer output from a valid clean review, so they may report/pass an incomplete review.

findings.title: Reject malformed review payloads
findings.whyItBreaks: Missing or wrongly typed required fields now become empty strings/arrays. For example, `{ "summary": "ok" }` is accepted as a no-findings review instead of surfacing the malformed reviewer response, so consumers cannot distinguish an invalid response from a legitimate empty review.

findings.title: Resolve the selected PR refs for manual dispatch
findings.whyItBreaks: A workflow_dispatch payload has no pull_request object. For the documented manual path, the checkout therefore falls back to github.ref, BASE_REF falls back to main, and both PR SHA variables are empty; the supplied pr_number no longer determines the checked-out revision or comparison refs. A manually dispatched review of a PR on another head/base can consequently run unrelated source and lack the target revisions.

findings.title: Restore PR-ref resolution for manual dispatch
findings.whyItBreaks: For workflow_dispatch, the event has no pull_request payload. This expression therefore falls back to github.ref (the workflow's selected branch), not the required pr_number's head. The changed workflow also supplies empty PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA at lines 45-46. Consequently, manually dispatching the explicitly supported PR-review workflow reviews from the dispatch branch without the requested PR comparison refs.

findings.title: Restore PR ref resolution for manual dispatch
findings.whyItBreaks: `workflow_dispatch` has no `pull_request` payload. Consequently both variables are empty, while checkout uses the independently selected dispatch ref rather than the requested `pr_number`'s head. A manual run can therefore review the wrong revision (usually the selected/default branch) with no valid base/head diff bounds. The removed step previously resolved all three values through `gh pr view` when the event payload was absent.

findings.title: Preserve the large buffer for git diff output
findings.whyItBreaks: `runLocal` obtains the entire patch through `git(["diff", baseSha, "HEAD"])` at line 100. This removal changes its capacity from 64 MiB to `spawnSync`’s default 1 MiB; a larger patch causes `spawnSync` to fail and the wrapper throws instead of producing a review.

findings.title: Preserve the 64 MiB buffer for Git output
findings.whyItBreaks: Omitting maxBuffer makes spawnSync use Node’s 1 MiB default. runLocal collects the complete patch through git(["diff", baseSha, "HEAD"]) at line 100, so a valid review diff larger than 1 MiB now terminates with a buffer error instead of producing a review. The previous 64 MiB limit explicitly supported these inputs.

findings.title: Restore the git output buffer limit
findings.whyItBreaks: Without maxBuffer, spawnSync uses Node's 1,048,576-byte stdout/stderr limit. runLocal obtains the full PR patch through this helper at line 100, so a diff over 1 MiB terminates git and throws before any review result is produced. The previous 64 MiB limit specifically supported these inputs.

findings.title: Bind the PR diff to GITHUB_REPOSITORY
findings.whyItBreaks: `gh pr diff` resolves its repository from the process working directory unless `--repo` is supplied, but this adapter's target repository is explicitly `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` and its supplied `cwd` may differ from that directory. The review can therefore fail outside a repository or analyze a same-numbered PR from another local repository.

findings.title: Keep a failed review check failing
findings.whyItBreaks: When `review()` throws, this publishes a `neutral` Needlefish check even though the error message says the PR did not pass. GitHub accepts neutral conclusions for required status checks, so a protected branch requiring Needlefish can be merged after the review failed.

findings.title: Keep review failures blocking
findings.whyItBreaks: GitHub accepts a completed neutral check as successful for required-check protection. When review() throws, this reports Needlefish as neutral even though the process says the PR was not reviewed, allowing a PR requiring Needlefish to merge.

findings.title: Derive changed files from the PR
findings.whyItBreaks: The patch now comes from the requested remote PR, but changedFiles still compares baseSha with the local checkout's HEAD. If cwd is not checked out at that PR head, the bundle describes one diff while its file surfaces and changedPaths describe another; findings on PR-only paths are then misclassified and excluded from inline comments.

findings.title: Keep review errors blocking
findings.whyItBreaks: When review execution or posting fails, this emits a completed "neutral" Needlefish check. GitHub treats neutral as a successful required status check, so a branch requiring Needlefish can merge although no successful review was produced.

findings.title: Restore the trusted checkout before executing the reviewer
findings.whyItBreaks: The checkout at lines 43-47 is the PR head, so this command executes PR-controlled src/cli.ts while GH_TOKEN is explicitly available and has pull-requests:write and checks:write permissions. Any same-repository PR author can alter the reviewer to forge or suppress review/check output and run arbitrary code on the self-hosted runner.

findings.title: Do not invoke tool files absent from this repository
findings.whyItBreaks: The head tree contains only .github/workflows/review.yml and .needlefish/answers.json: it has no package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, src/cli.ts, or tsx dependency. After checkout, ./node_modules/.bin/tsx and src/cli.ts therefore do not exist, so every future review job fails instead of publishing a review.

findings.whyItBreaks: The PR head is now the workspace checkout, so pnpm install consumes its package metadata and lifecycle hooks and tsx executes its src/cli.ts. A same-repository PR can therefore replace either with arbitrary code running on the self-hosted runner with GH_TOKEN, whose workflow permissions include pull-requests: write and checks: write. An internal PR can alter the reviewer or add lifecycle code to make its own review pass or execute arbitrary runner commands; the previous workflow deliberately isolated the tool at frankekn/needlefish@main.

The root pnpm install cannot install the reviewer, and the subsequent ./node_modules/.bin/tsx src/cli.ts command cannot exist, so every eligible review job fails before producing a review.

findings.title: Preserve canonical severity normalization
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview accepts untyped JSON and passes each finding to this function. A valid severity such as "p1" or " P1 " was previously normalized to P1, but now fails the case-sensitive membership check and is emitted as P3, silently downclassifying the finding.

findings.title: Normalize severity text before applying the fallback
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview accepts untyped raw output and passes each finding to normalizeFinding. A semantically valid JSON value such as " p0 " or "p1" previously canonicalized to P0/P1, but now fails the exact-match check and is silently emitted as P3, under-reporting the finding's severity.

findings.title: Normalize severity strings before validating them
findings.whyItBreaks: `normalizeReview` accepts untyped review JSON, so a finding severity such as `" p0 "` or `"p0"` previously normalized to `P0` but now fails the exact-membership check and is emitted as `P3`. This silently downgrades critical findings.

findings.title: Keep GitHub credentials out of the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: Omitting `env` makes `spawnSync` inherit `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and `GITHUB_API_TOKEN`. The reviewed Codex process and any commands it invokes can now read credentials that the previous implementation explicitly removed, permitting token exfiltration or authenticated GitHub actions from an untrusted review context.

findings.title: Keep GitHub credentials out of the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the explicit env object makes spawnSync inherit process.env, including GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN. The Codex process handling the supplied prompt and repository can now access credentials that the previous code intentionally withheld.

findings.title: Keep GitHub credentials out of the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: Without an env option, spawnSync inherits process.env. This passes GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN to the Codex process while it handles the supplied prompt and repository, undoing the prior explicit secret boundary. The read-only sandbox limits filesystem actions; it does not remove inherited credentials from the subprocess.

findings.title: Restore the same-repository gate before executing PR code
findings.whyItBreaks: Fork PRs now enter this job, which checks out the fork-controlled SHA (line 23), installs its dependency graph (line 28), and executes its fork-controlled src/cli.ts (line 34) on a self-hosted runner. A fork author can therefore obtain arbitrary code execution in the runner environment.

findings.title: Restore the fork-origin guard before running PR code
findings.whyItBreaks: Fork PRs now schedule this self-hosted job. The workflow checks out the attacker-controlled head SHA at line 23 and executes its src/cli.ts at line 34, allowing arbitrary code execution as the runner account and persistent compromise of the runner environment.

findings.title: Restore the fork restriction for the self-hosted review job
findings.whyItBreaks: Fork PRs now enter this self-hosted job, which explicitly checks out the fork-controlled head SHA and executes its dependency installation and src/cli.ts. A contributor can therefore submit a fork whose code executes on the runner, exposing runner-resident credentials, network access, and persistent workspace state.

findings.title: Preserve zero-valued runner timeout delays
findings.whyItBreaks: A configured value of "0" previously produced a zero-delay timer. It now falls back to 5000 ms for NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS or 2000 ms for NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS. Existing deployments using zero to request immediate SIGKILL escalation or immediate completion after SIGKILL will instead wait several seconds.

findings.title: Accept zero-duration runner settings
findings.whyItBreaks: The prior parser explicitly accepted finite non-negative durations, so existing deployments using either runner duration environment variable with "0" lose their configured behavior after upgrade. NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 now waits 5000ms before SIGKILL rather than escalating immediately; NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 now waits 2000ms before returning instead of giving up immediately.

findings.title: Preserve zero-duration runner settings
findings.whyItBreaks: A configured value of "0" previously remained 0, allowing immediate escalation after the runner timeout. It now becomes the fallback value, adding 5 seconds for NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS or 2 seconds for NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS.

findings.title: Restore coverage for unmapped changed files
findings.whyItBreaks: Large reviews process only the first six mapped hotspots. Removing the tail hotspot means any changed file omitted by those hotspots is never sent to the deep reviewer, so defects in that file can receive a clean review result.

findings.title: Preserve deep-review residual risks
findings.whyItBreaks: Every deep review's residual_risks value is discarded and replaced with []. A deep reviewer can therefore report an unresolved blocking risk, but the critic receives the same payload as for a clean review and cannot preserve that failure signal.

findings.title: Convert failed deep passes into blocking results
findings.whyItBreaks: A malformed or failed deep-review call now rejects reviewLarge immediately. Previously that hotspot was recorded as a blocking residual risk and the caller still received a ReviewResult identifying the unreviewed files.

findings.title: Restore coverage for every changed file
findings.whyItBreaks: After capping to six hotspots, the deep-review loop only processes those selected hotspots. Files omitted by the mapper, or assigned to a seventh-or-later hotspot, now have no deep pass at all; their defects can be omitted from the merged review.

findings.title: Forward deep-review residual risks
findings.whyItBreaks: A deep pass can report a blocking residual risk, but candidateMerged now replaces all such signals with an empty array before invoking the critic. The critic therefore cannot distinguish a fully reviewed large PR from one with unresolved deep-review evidence and may return a pass without that block.

findings.title: Keep coverage for every changed file
findings.whyItBreaks: The map result is accepted when it contains any hotspot, but only the selected hotspots are deep-reviewed. Removing the uncovered-file tail means a mapper response that omits a changed file leaves that file without a deep pass, allowing its defects to be absent from the merged review.

findings.title: Preserve deep-review blocking residual risks
findings.whyItBreaks: Each deep review can return residual risks that block a verdict, but candidateMerged now replaces all of them with an empty array. The critic therefore cannot receive a known blocker from a completed deep pass, and the final verdict can be derived without that blocker.

findings.title: Restore focus and deep forwarding for large reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: reviewSmall still serializes the complete Bundle, but reviewLarge now omits focus and deep from mapBundle and no longer substitutes bundle.focus into each deep prompt. A caller requesting a focused/deep review of a patch above the large-review threshold receives an unscoped review instead, so the requested surface can be missed solely because the patch is large.

findings.title: Restore focus propagation for large reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: When a bundle exceeds the large-patch threshold, review() routes it to reviewLarge(), but this path now omits bundle.focus from the map payload and no longer substitutes it into each deep-review prompt. A caller requesting a focused review therefore receives an unfocused large review, while small reviews still serialize the complete bundle including focus.

findings.title: Preserve focus in large-review prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: The deep-review prompt no longer substitutes bundle.focus, and the map bundle no longer includes it. Consequently, any non-empty focus supplied for a large patch never reaches either review stage, unlike reviewSmall which serializes the complete Bundle. Targeted large reviews therefore review the default scope instead of the requested area.

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into minutes
findings.whyItBreaks: For 119500ms, minutes is floored to 1 while the remainder rounds to 60, so rendered statistics show "1m 60s" instead of "2m 0s".

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into minutes
findings.whyItBreaks: For 119500 ms, this computes minutes=1 and seconds=60, so rendered review output says "1m 60s" instead of the correctly normalized "2m 0s". The formatter is used for per-call and total durations.

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into minutes
findings.whyItBreaks: For durations from 59,500ms through 59,999ms, `seconds` rounds to 60 while `minutes` remains 0, rendering `60s` instead of `1m 0s`. At later boundaries this produces values such as `1m 60s`. The previous implementation rounded the total duration before deriving minutes, so it normalized these boundaries.

findings.title: Reject zero in parsePositiveInteger
findings.whyItBreaks: `0` now passes the guard and is returned, although both the exported symbol and its error contract promise a positive integer. Public callers can therefore receive a value outside the documented domain.

findings.title: Reject zero to preserve the positive-integer contract
findings.whyItBreaks: `parsePositiveInteger("0", label)` now returns `0`, although both its exported name and thrown-error contract promise a positive integer. External callers can therefore receive a value outside the API's stated range.

findings.title: Keep zero out of the positive-integer parser
findings.whyItBreaks: `parsePositiveInteger("0", label)` now returns `0`, although its exported name and thrown error promise a positive integer. Public callers can rely on this parser to reject zero and subsequently receive an invalid value.
